chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The thief's hand is not cut off during a year of famine, meaning during a year of scarcity.
ai.seo_question: When is the hand of a thief not cut off according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of *al-maslahah* (public interest) in Shia jurisprudence, where the harshness of the fixed punishment (*hadd*) is relaxed during times of widespread scarcity to prevent further hardship. It reflects the Imams' pragmatic approach to law, prioritizing the welfare of the community over rigid application of penalties when the root cause of theft is economic distress. This ruling underscores the flexibility within *fiqh* to adapt legal outcomes to changing social and economic conditions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The thief would not be cut during a year of inactivity, meaning during a year of famine’.
